title: Rearchitect continuous enqueue/scheduler handoff and KV staleness protector
creator: Marcelo Li
description: This ticket targets a multi-part refactor of the continuous-batching enqueue path and the scheduler handoff to reduce tail latency, eliminate transient KV cache staleness, and remove a set of platform spinlocks that cause jitter under hotkey load. The current controller mixes admission, prefetch, and slot allocation in a single state machine which complicates backpressure reasoning and makes KV lease expiry brittle during heavy churn. Goal: split responsibilities, introduce deterministic handoff semantics, and add a KV staleness protector (time+lease based) so in-flight requests never read evicted entries unexpectedly.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler handoff follows a documented deterministic contract: enqueue -> staging queue -> slot assignment -> dispatch. No more shared mutable state across these steps.
KV staleness protector prevents stale reads observed in incident-2025-11 and reduces KV-related 5xx by >=90% in the canary region.
End-to-end p99 latency for chat generation under synthetic hotkey test reduced by at least 15% compared to baseline (same traffic profile).
All runtime unit and integration tests pass; new regression tests added for lease expiry windows and concurrent evictions.
Migration/rollback path defined with feature flag and canary rollout plan documented in the ticket.
technical_decisions: Introduce a two-queue handoff: fast in-memory staging ring (lock-free MPSC) + deterministic slot allocator that owns KV lease lifecycle.
Replace coarse spinlocks in admission code with async-aware semaphores / parking_lot guards where necessary to avoid thread parking under GPU-bound workloads.
KV staleness protector implemented as: lease token (sequence+expiry) attached to cache entries and validated on read; fallback to prefetch if token expired but entry still present.
Upgrade async runtime from tokio 1.27 -> 1.31 to pick up task::yield and scheduling improvements; audit all await points to avoid `.block_in_place()` in hot paths.
Keep public RPC contract (ingress API) unchanged; introduce a per-node feature flag to enable new handoff semantics for canary before cluster-wide rollout.
steps: 1) Prototype two-queue handoff and slot allocator in a feature branch with microbenchmarks (owner: Priya).
2) Implement KV lease tokens and add read-path validation + graceful prefetch fallback (owner: Aisha Kapoor).
3) Replace problematic spinlocks and run stress tests under hotkey traffic (owner: Tomas Nguyen).
4) Integrate dependency upgrades in separate PRs: tokio, parking_lot; ensure no semver breaks (owner: Marcelo).
5) Add regression tests and chaos test for concurrent eviction/read races; run on scale QA cluster (owner: Priya).
6) Canary rollout to eu-west-1 with 5% traffic and close monitoring of error budgets, tail latency, and KV metrics; collect dashboards and compare to baseline.
7) Incremental ramp with automatic rollback on violation of SLOs; finalize rollout if stable for 72h.
notes: This work is driven by repeated incidents (see incident-2025-11) where KV entries were observed being read shortly after eviction due to race between prefetch and eviction path.
We must be careful with memory amplification in the staging ring; keep per-item footprint small (token + pointer + 8B flags).
Performance trade-off: stronger safety (lease checks) may add a few CPU cycles on hot path; mitigate via inlined token checks and avoid allocations.
